nodes.description: A patent publication titled "Social medical network for diagnosis assistance" describing a method for diagnosis assistance using similarity between medical cases and experts in a common embedding space.

nodes.entity_id: Social Medical Network For Diagnosis Assistance
nodes.description: The title of the patent US9589231B2, referring to a network-based approach for assisting medical diagnosis.
nodes.id: Social Medical Network For Diagnosis Assistance

nodes.description: A method that exploits similarity between a new medical case and existing medical cases and experts embedded in a common embedding space, supporting query-by-cases and query-by-experts.

A common space in which a new medical case, existing medical cases, and experts are embedded as multidimensional representations used to compute similarity.<SEP>A multidimensional space in which new medical cases, existing medical cases, and experts are embedded as multidimensional representations.

A medical case submitted by a requester in a query request, which is embedded in the embedding space for comparison with existing cases and experts.<SEP>A case comprising a plurality of records relating to a specific patient, received in a query request and embedded in the embedding space for diagnosis assistance.

A set of previously known medical cases embedded in the embedding space, used as candidates returned in a query-for-cases.<SEP>A set of medical cases that are embedded in the embedding space and compared against a new medical case via a computed similarity.

A set of medical experts embedded in the embedding space, used as candidates returned in a query-for-experts to attempt to provide a diagnosis.<SEP>A set of experts each embedded in the embedding space based on information such as expert profiles, coded medical procedures performed, authored articles, and stored medical cases linked to the expert.
The party submitting a query request including a new medical case and selecting from available query types.<SEP>A user who submits a request for a query including a new medical case.

A query type that returns a subset of existing medical cases based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.<SEP>A query type in which a subset of existing cases is returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.

A query type that returns a subset of experts based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts.<SEP>A query type in which a subset of experts is returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts.

A computed cost for a query, where the cost for a query-for-experts differs from and is higher than the cost for a query-for-cases.<SEP>A computed cost for a query, where the cost for a query-for-experts differs from the cost for a query-for-cases.

A set of medical concepts joined by links, each concept corresponding to a dimension in the multidimensional representation, used as the basis for embedding cases and experts.<SEP>An ontology that includes parts of the human body, biological functions, medical conditions, pharmacological substances, and combinations thereof, and may be based on the Unified Medical Language System.
Concepts within the medical ontology joined by links, each corresponding to a respective dimension in the representation.
A computed representation of a medical case based on the medical ontology, used for embedding in the embedding space.

A matrix applied to the multidimensional representation of the new case that accounts for relationships between concepts in the ontology when computing similarity.<SEP>A matrix applied to the multidimensional representation of the new case that accounts for relationships between concepts in the ontology when computing the similarity measure.
One of the categories of concepts included in the medical ontology.
One of the categories of concepts included in the medical ontology.
One of the categories of concepts included in the medical ontology.
One of the categories of concepts included in the medical ontology.
A processor used to perform at least one of the embedding, providing, returning subsets, and computing query cost steps of the method.
A medical ontology system on which the medical ontology used in the method is based.

A system comprising memory storing instructions and a processor for executing them, used to receive query requests, embed new medical cases, return subsets of cases or experts, and compute query costs.
A set of devices in a network for linking requesters and experts with the diagnosis assistance system.
A network comprising a diagnosis assistance system and a set of user devices for linking requesters and experts with the system.
A product comprising a non-transitory recording medium storing instructions that, when executed on a computer, cause the computer to perform the method of claim 1.
A diagnosis formulated by a selected expert to whom a new case is provided.
A payment made to an expert for formulating a diagnosis.
A database from which documents are returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and documents embedded in the embedding space.

edges.description: The patent publication US9589231B2 describes a method for diagnosis assistance.
The diagnosis assistance method embeds a new medical case, existing medical cases, and experts in a common embedding space.
The method receives a query request including a new medical case and embeds the new medical case in the embedding space.
The method computes similarity between the embedded new case and embedded existing medical cases to return a subset of the cases.
The method computes similarity between the embedded new case and embedded experts to return a subset of the experts.
The method provides for the requester to select a query-for-cases type that returns a subset of existing cases.
The method provides for the requester to select a query-for-experts type that returns a subset of experts.
The method computes a cost for the query, with the query-for-experts cost differing from the query-for-cases cost.
The embedding of the new case, existing cases, and experts is based on a medical ontology.
At least one of the embedding, providing, returning subsets, and computing query cost steps is performed with a computer processor.
The new medical case is embedded in the embedding space in which existing medical cases and experts are also embedded.
The set of existing medical cases is embedded in the embedding space.
The set of experts is embedded in the embedding space.
The requester submits a query request that includes a new medical case.<SEP>The requester submits a request for a query that includes a new medical case.
The diagnosis assistance system receives a query request including a new medical case and embeds the new medical case in the embedding space.
The matrix of proximities is applied to the multidimensional representation of the new case to account for relationships between concepts in the ontology.
Documents from a public database are returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and documents embedded in the embedding space.
When the query-for-cases is selected, a subset of the existing cases is returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.
When the query-for-experts is selected, a subset of the experts is returned based on a computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts.
The user devices link experts with the diagnosis assistance system.
A selected one of the subset of experts is provided the new case for formulating a diagnosis.
A payment is made to the expert for formulating the diagnosis.
The requester may select the query-for-cases query type.<SEP>The requester is provided for to select from a plurality of query types including a query-for-cases and a query-for-experts.
The requester may select the query-for-experts query type.<SEP>The requester is provided for to select from a plurality of query types including a query-for-cases and a query-for-experts.
The user devices link requesters with the diagnosis assistance system.
The computed query cost is lower for a query-for-cases than for a query-for-experts.<SEP>The cost for a query-for-cases differs from the cost for a query-for-experts.
The diagnosis assistance system provides for the requester to select from a plurality of query types including a query-for-cases.
The computed query cost is higher for a query-for-experts than for a query-for-cases.<SEP>The cost for a query-for-experts is different from the cost for a query-for-cases.
The diagnosis assistance system provides for the requester to select from a plurality of query types including a query-for-experts.
The diagnosis assistance system computes a cost for the query, with the cost for a query-for-experts being different from the cost for a query-for-cases.
